PullRequest.Title: policy: preserve managed sandbox force-on for Agent Host routing
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334273

## Summary
- Resolve managed `sandbox.enabled` with force-on semantics: `true` from any device, server, or file source wins. Other managed settings retain existing precedence.
- Feed the corrected value into existing Agent Host Copilot default/preference routing so a higher-priority `false` cannot hide a sandbox requirement.
- Update diagnostics and provenance documentation; cover all 27 absent/false/true source combinations, malformed values, and policy refresh/removal through harness selection.

Existing routing exceptions, existing sessions, and non-local harness selections remain unchanged. Runtime enforcement and `sandbox.allowBypass` composition are outside this change.

Release counterpart: #334652 (targets `release/1.137`). This PR contains the original fix commit against `main`.

## Validation
On this main-based commit:
- Client transpilation passed.
- All 98 focused resolver, account policy, Agent Host enablement, and chat routing tests passed.
- ESLint, hygiene, and whitespace checks passed.

The identical cherry-pick on `release/1.137` additionally passed the client type check. Full compilation on the release branch stopped at an unrelated Monaco declaration freshness check; generated changes were not included in either branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and managed-policy refresh merge native MDM, server, and file settings into AccountPolicyService state.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Native policy definition initialization may complete before AccountPolicyService recomputes policy values; the changed pickManagedSettings branch is synchronous in-memory work on that path. File and server data are already held by their services when this merge runs. The force-remote-refresh network path is governed by a different key and is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize/update native managed-setting definitions through the main-process policy watcher channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one IPC call for each existing AccountPolicyService definition-update invocation; native watcher updates are serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same definition-update IPC occurred before this PR; the diff only changes one in-memory key-resolution rule after values are available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: AccountPolicyService awaits this existing call before resolving policy values.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the bounded managed-settings.json file after startup or coalesced file-change notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per coalesced refresh, capped at 1 MB; not one read per key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same independently scheduled file read populated the same bag before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial service snapshot can precede policy resolution, but subsequent AccountPolicyService merges consume cached in-memory data.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch server-delivered managed settings during DefaultAccount refresh, potentially retrying across available authentication sessions until a terminal response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per attempted authentication session on an existing account refresh, with existing rate-limit backoff; no request is issued by pickManagedSettings itself.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same account refresh and request loop existed before the PR; sandbox force-on only changes the effective cached boolean.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A required force-remote-refresh can make this existing fetch startup-critical, but that is controlled by COPILOT_FORCE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_REFRESH_KEY, whose resolution is unchanged by the sandbox-specific branch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K distinct managed-setting keys across at most three fixed delivery channels. The new condition executes only for duplicate contributions and remains O(K), with no new allocation proportional to history or events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The resolver is single-threaded and scans the three bags once. Native watcher initialization is serialized by its existing Throttler/initialization promise; file changes are coalesced by the existing 500 ms ThrottledDelayer. The diff changes neither scheduling nor concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All three inputs are in-memory snapshots at merge time. Native initialization promises and file IPC snapshots are reused, unchanged values are suppressed with equals, and no cache key or invalidation behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk adds only constant-time comparisons and assignments inside the existing bounded merge; repository callers and source services show no added boundary call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Managed-setting bag sizes vary by enterprise schema, but the number of channels is fixed at three and the added primitive comparisons are negligible relative to pre-existing projection and policy evaluation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR preserves the existing one-pass merge and boundary cardinality while changing only the winning sandbox value/source.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or resetting a chat after conflicting managed sources now selects Agent Host Copilot when any source requires sandboxing.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Policy refresh publishes an in-memory observable. New-chat selection synchronously reads that boolean and chooses a session URI; actual Agent Host session creation occurs later when the selected chat session is materialized and is then on the chat-start critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an Agent Host session through the existing agent-host connection for a newly selected AgentHostCopilot chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing createSession operation for the newly materialized Agent Host chat session; no operation occurs merely from recomputing the policy observable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A higher-precedence false could select the local harness instead, so this subset of managed users did not enter the required Agent Host session path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For the conflicting-source configuration fixed by this PR, chat startup follows the Agent Host path required to honor managed sandboxing. Cold host startup may be slower than a warm connection, but there is no per-key or per-source boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One routing decision per new/reset chat; policy-source count does not multiply session creation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection is synchronous and constant-time. Agent Host creation remains the existing per-session path; this PR does not add parallel creation, fan-out, or a new listener.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The effective sandbox value is retained in AccountPolicyService and exposed through an event-backed observable. Warm Agent Host reuse is owned by the existing Agent Host service; the diff neither invalidates nor bypasses it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that routing changes for a realistic false/true source conflict and reaches the existing Agent Host createSession boundary; low evidence that this safety-required route is an avoidable performance degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cold-versus-warm cost of an Agent Host session is not quantified, and local-harness relative cost is not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue. The one-per-session boundary is the intended mechanism for enforcing the managed sandbox contract, with no evidence of redundant work or a bounded alternative that preserves enforcement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running the Policy Diagnostics developer action displays sandbox force-on provenance.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The manually invoked action reads cached managed-setting bags, runs the same in-memory merge/projection, builds Markdown, and opens the diagnostics result. The changed static explanatory text and effective value computation are on this explicit command path only.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of declared and supplied managed-setting keys. The new sandbox comparison is constant per duplicate contribution and the added diagnostic sentence has fixed size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single command execution; no new asynchronous work, limiter, queue, or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The action consumes existing cached source snapshots. It neither refreshes sources nor changes cache lifetime or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the action diff changes only a fixed Markdown sentence; shared resolver behavior adds no boundary operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Diagnostic schemas can vary in size, but the added work is fixed/linear within an already explicit developer-only command.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. The runtime change is a bounded constant-time override inside an existing O(K) three-source merge. Traced startup/refresh, chat routing, and diagnostics scenarios found no new repeated work, retention, concurrency burst, or avoidable boundary fan-out. No performance findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
